Michael Z., a Senior Account Executive, had a choice before going on vacation:

1. Spend hours queuing emails and hoping nothing slipped
2. Accept that his pipeline would slow down
3. Or test something new

He chose option 3.

Before heading to the Bahamas, he set up AI agents inside Outreach to keep his pipeline.

No crossed fingers. Just continuous execution in the background.

Here’s how he used them:
Always-on prospecting → Conversations keep starting, even when he’s not working
Automated follow-ups → No dropped threads or missed timing
PTO coverage → Meetings booked while he’s off the grid

The result? His vacation started. His pipeline didn't. Two meetings booked while he was away.

“The goal isn’t just saving time, it’s making sure nothing stalls.”

Once you see it working, it changes your baseline.
Because the real question becomes: Why should pipeline ever depend on your availability in the first place?

I have a drawer at home full of cables I can't identify and refuse to throw away. VGA. PS/2. That little purple keyboard connector. Sound familiar?

For 20 years, every device needed its own port. Then USB-C showed up and... one plug, everything just works.

That's the exact shift happening right now with AI and your GTM stack, and it's what I unpacked in our latest webinar, MCP & Outreach.

Here's the short version: Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT, Gemini, whatever your team already uses, used to need a custom, one-off integration to see your Outreach data. Its own cable, its own port, every time.

MCP changes that. One connector. One standard. Every AI tool you already own just plugs in.

In the recording, I get specific on:
⚡ When MCP is the right call (and when it isn't)
⚡ What Outreach Agents do that a connector alone never will
🔐 How RevOps can roll this out without losing sleep over governance
💼 Real examples for sellers, sales leaders, and RevOps, not just theory

posts.content:
Watching Spain lift the World Cup last week, one thought stayed with me. 

Plenty will be written about the players, the tactics, and the moments that decided it. But what stayed with me was something less visible. 

The best teams reduce the number of things they leave to chance. 

Players don't have to rediscover how to respond every time the game changes. Preparation, judgment, and coordination are built into how the team operates. 

That is an important distinction for business. 

For decades, companies have tried to improve performance by hiring exceptional people and giving them better software. Yet the quality of execution still varies enormously from one person, one deal, and one day to the next. 

The real opportunity isn't simply to add AI. 

It's to embed the preparation, context, and next-best actions of your strongest performers directly into the flow of work - so that great execution becomes more consistent across the entire team. 

That's what we're building at Outreach. 

Not software that simply watches the game. 

AI agents that help revenue teams play it better.
